c.tagline: A small capital where volcanoes, ice, and aurora collide.

taxi.fareNote: Starting fare around ISK 700 (~$5) plus a per-km rate; cards accepted everywhere; no tipping expected.

emergency.note: Iceland uses a single nationwide emergency number, 112, for police, medical, and fire; English-speaking operators are available and there is also a 112 Iceland safety-check app for travelers.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The Laugavegur bar strip gets rowdy with drunken crowds late on weekend nights; otherwise the city is exceptionally safe.

hood_desc: The historic downtown core packed with restaurants, bars, shops and Hallgrímskirkja church; ideal for first-time visitors who want to walk to everything.

A revitalized waterfront of old fish-processing warehouses turned into design studios, breweries, and the Maritime Museum; suits foodies and those catching whale-watching or Golden Circle tours nearby.
The main shopping street and its eastern end around the Hlemmur food hall, full of vintage shops, cafes and nightlife; great for younger travelers wanting energy after dark.
A leafy park district with Iceland's largest geothermal pool, a zoo and botanical garden; ideal for families and budget travelers using the campsite/hostel.
A quiet, residential seaside neighborhood near the university and domestic airport with a beloved local pool; suited to travelers wanting a local, low-key base a short walk from downtown.

water.note: Naturally pure spring-sourced tap water, safe to drink straight from the tap with no treatment needed.

transit.pay: Most riders pay via the Klapp app, which offers tap-to-pay virtual tickets and pre-paid trip bundles. Contactless bank cards can also be tapped on validators on many routes. Exact cash is accepted onboard but drivers give no change.
transit.hours: Most routes run roughly 6:30/7:00 AM to midnight on weekdays with reduced evening and Sunday frequency; there is no true late-night or 24-hour bus service.
transit.note: Reykjavík has no metro, tram, or train — Strætó buses are the only public transit system; the compact city center is very walkable, and renting a car is common for day trips outside town.

ferry: Viðey Island ferry (from Reykjavík Old Harbour)

transit.m: Flybus coach to BSÍ terminal (~45 min)
Strætó public bus route 55 (~1 hr, budget option)

tip.r: Service charge is included in restaurant and bar prices; tipping is not expected, though rounding up or a small tip for exceptional service is appreciated.
